editorial:
Imagine a world where martial arts movies just wanted to be fun and loud. You get exactly that here, where a scientist's daughter is snatched by bad guys, and the only person who can save her is a seasoned ninja. But there is a cool twist this time around. Instead of going solo, he brings along a young student he has been training. It feels like a classic buddy movie mixed with high-energy fight scenes. The vibe is very 90s, with plenty of leather gear, dramatic poses, and that specific kind of action that makes you want to grab some popcorn and just turn your brain off for a while.

What really works is the chemistry between the master and the student, which adds a bit of heart to all the punching and kicking. The pacing is quick, though some of the acting can be a bit cheesy. If you love old-school fights and don't mind some silly plot holes, you will have a blast. To get the best experience, you should look for the 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for those crisp colors. If you are in a rush, renting it on Apple TV is a great way to see if you like it before buying.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with a big final showdown where the ninja and his student take on the villains to rescue the daughter. After a series of intense fights, they manage to defeat the main boss and save the girl just in time. The story ends on a positive note, showing that the student has finally mastered his skills and earned the respect of his teacher through his bravery.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 90s action movies and martial arts battles.
